title: Niagara

jokes.text: Jim talking head: 'A three-ounce fetus is calling the shots. It's so badass.'
jokes.setup: Jim describes Pam's pregnancy nausea forcing office-wide accommodations
jokes.punchline: He reframes the fetus as a tiny tyrant with admiration — 'It's so badass'
jokes.explanation: This is genuinely excellent. The reframe of a fetus as a badass power broker is unexpected, the economy is perfect, and it's completely in Jim's voice — bemused pride mixed with dry observation. 'It's so badass' as the punchline lands with perfect understatement. Comparable in quality to the 8.0 anchor.

jokes.text: Phyllis: 'Now this is getting ridiculous. Oh gee, I'm sorry. I guess I missed the meeting where we all voted for you to get pregnant.'
jokes.setup: Pam asks Phyllis to switch soap brands due to pregnancy nausea
jokes.punchline: Phyllis fires back with mock-apologetic sarcasm about the 'meeting' to vote on Pam's pregnancy
jokes.explanation: Phyllis getting a sharp comeback is a nice subversion — she's usually passive. The 'meeting' framing is a smart office-context joke. Good character work.

jokes.text: Creed: 'I reserve the right to peel my hardboiled eggs at my desk.'
jokes.setup: Pam is making increasingly unreasonable requests about smells in the office
jokes.punchline: Creed, completely unprompted, stakes his territorial claim about hardboiled eggs as if it were a constitutional right
jokes.explanation: Classic Creed — completely specific, totally committed, utterly weird. The word 'right' does enormous work, giving it legal gravitas. Nobody else in the cast could deliver this. Maximum character integration, perfect economy. One of the cold open's best beats.

jokes.text: Dwight talking head: 'All morning I look forward to my afternoon cigars, and I am not stopping for anybody.'
jokes.setup: Office staff are being asked to accommodate Pam's pregnancy-related smell sensitivities
jokes.punchline: Dwight declares cigar loyalty with the conviction of a man defending a sacred ritual
jokes.explanation: Functional Dwight character beat but doesn't transcend the setup. The cigars detail is specific but the joke is essentially just 'Dwight is stubborn,' which we already know.

jokes.text: Toby talking head: 'Watching people get sick always makes me sick. And...well, frankly, so does talking about it, so...' [trails off]
jokes.setup: Toby begins a confessional apparently about Pam's pregnancy
jokes.punchline: He trails off mid-sentence, unable to finish because even talking about it nauseates him — the joke IS the incomplete thought
jokes.explanation: Beautiful Toby moment — the trailing off IS the punchline. His inability to complete even a talking-head confessional is peak sad-sack Toby. The ellipsis does the work. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Jim's face/reaction when he sees what Dwight did — Dwight apparently decorated Jim's body or clothing, spending 'all morning' on it. Jim's resigned 'Yeah, but aren't you supposed to do that to our-- no, it's great.'
jokes.setup: Dwight proudly announces he spent all morning doing something 'really special' for Jim and Pam's wedding day
jokes.punchline: Jim's visibly pained non-reaction and half-objection ('aren't you supposed to do that to our--') before giving up — whatever Dwight did is clearly wrong/inappropriate
jokes.explanation: A classic Jim-Dwight visual beat where the specifics are funnier for being unclear. Jim's instinct to correct Dwight, then his resignation ('no, it's great'), is perfectly in character. Rewatch bonus because the visual gag pays off more on revisit.

jokes.text: Kevin objects to no firecrackers at the wedding. Michael: 'So you're gonna provide them then?' Kevin: 'No, this is a firecracker-free wedding.' Kevin: 'What the hell?'
jokes.setup: Pam reads through the wedding rules, emphasizing that firecrackers are in the 'don't' column
jokes.punchline: Kevin is genuinely outraged by no firecrackers at a wedding, treating it as a personal affront
jokes.explanation: Classic Kevin — childlike indignation at missing out on something clearly inappropriate. 'What the hell?' as genuine grievance about wedding firecrackers is good character comedy.

jokes.text: Angela: 'Well, you're lucky to have a grandmother. Some of us have to be our own grandmother.'
jokes.setup: Pam explains she wants to protect her conservative grandmother from news of the pregnancy
jokes.punchline: Angela pivots to a darkly self-pitying non-sequitur about having to be her own grandmother
jokes.explanation: This is one of the best lines in the episode. 'Some of us have to be our own grandmother' is a genuinely surreal, quotable Angela line that reveals her lonely rigidity while being absurdly funny. It makes no literal sense and perfect character sense simultaneously. High originality, economy is flawless, deeply Angela. Justifies the 8+ score.

jokes.text: Dwight pinches Jim as he's leaving — Jim reports 'He pinched me' to camera
jokes.setup: The group says their goodbyes before heading to Niagara
jokes.punchline: Dwight's farewell is a covert pinch; Jim's deadpan report to camera completes the joke
jokes.explanation: A quick, well-executed beat. Jim's matter-of-fact 'He pinched me' to camera is the whole joke and it works well — typical Dwight aggression expressed in the most petty possible form. Good economy.

jokes.text: Michael: 'What happens in Niagara stays in Niagara.' Then immediately claims Dwight stole his joke when Dwight says the same thing.
jokes.setup: Michael says the 'What happens in X stays in X' joke about Niagara Falls
jokes.punchline: He immediately polices Dwight for 'stealing' it, despite it being an obvious generic formula, then Dwight proves the point by applying it to 'accounting'
jokes.explanation: Good Michael moment — his desperate ownership of a totally non-original joke is perfectly in character. Dwight's 'What happens in accounting stays in accounting' escalation is a nice button. The meta-commentary on joke theft is mildly clever.

jokes.text: Michael's voicemail slip: 'I will see you up here in Viagra falls.'
jokes.setup: Michael records a voicemail message for Dunder Mifflin announcing the Niagara Falls wedding
jokes.punchline: He accidentally (or carelessly) says 'Viagra Falls' instead of 'Niagara Falls'
jokes.explanation: A predictable Niagara/Viagra slip but lands because it's Michael on a company voicemail. The joke itself is a familiar pun but the context (official Dunder Mifflin message) gives it a slight boost.

jokes.text: Dwight talking head: He stole Jim's guest list and 'search-engined every female on both sides of the family' as a wedding pickup strategy
jokes.setup: Dwight declares Jim and Pam's wedding will be 'the single best pickup destination in the history of the universe'
jokes.punchline: He reveals he has been systematically researching female wedding guests using stolen documents and internet searches
jokes.explanation: The methodical, military-operation approach to wedding flirtation is perfect Dwight. 'Search-engined' as a verb is delightful. The detail that he stole Jim's guest list adds a layer of violation that's darkly funny. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Dwight's intel on Pam's cousin Jocelyn: she was selling a mountain bike two years ago and 'is really into mountain biking but not so much lately'
jokes.setup: Dwight has researched wedding guests and dramatically reveals intel on a specific target
jokes.punchline: His 'intelligence' amounts to a two-year-old Craigslist or classifieds ad for a used bicycle — and his romantic interest is based solely on her spending habits
jokes.explanation: This escalation is beautifully constructed. The buildup to Dwight's 'intel' being a secondhand bike listing, concluded with 'if she was able to sell her bike, then...' as a romantic inference, is gloriously stupid and specific. Michael's flat 'You're an idiot' is the perfect button. Strong structure.

jokes.text: Kevin talking head about his wedding outfit: 'People don't think of me as one of the sharper dressers in the office, but I'm going to turn that around at this wedding... the hair. It's the hair.'
jokes.setup: Kevin confesses his plan to upgrade his image at the wedding
jokes.punchline: He reveals his entire strategy is a hairpiece — shown visually — which is clearly not the solution he thinks it is
jokes.explanation: Kevin's self-delusion is perfectly calibrated here. The pause before 'the hair' and then 'It's the hair' repeated with total conviction is great. The visual of the toupee presumably looking terrible is the payoff. Strong character integration — only Kevin would think a hairpiece solves his image problem.

jokes.text: Michael asks if someone wants to sit up front with him. Andy: 'Nah, this is so much cooler. We feel like we're in a limo and you're our driver.'
jokes.setup: Michael offers front-seat companionship on the 5-hour drive to Niagara
jokes.punchline: Andy reframes their avoidance as a luxury experience — they're in the back like VIPs with a chauffeur
jokes.explanation: Nice slight — the polite cruelty of calling Michael their 'driver' to his face while making it sound like a compliment is good. A bit obvious but well-executed.

jokes.text: Michael about Erin: 'Not only is Erin really sweet and cute... She smells like my mom.'
jokes.setup: Michael talks about why he's interested in Erin sitting with him
jokes.punchline: After setting up a normal attraction ('sweet and cute'), he adds the deeply weird 'She smells like my mom' as if it's an additional selling point
jokes.explanation: Classic Michael psychological reveal — his mother abandonment issues manifesting in the most casually disturbing way. The structure is perfect: normal setup, then the unexpected pivot to maternal scent as an attraction. Only Michael Scott could say this, and only The Office would treat it as a throwaway. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Jim's 'mental picture' bit: Pam's aunt's advice about taking mental pictures, Jim tries it, 'Click. Oh, you blinked. Damn it. Now that's in my brain forever. What a lousy picture.'
jokes.setup: Pam shares her aunt's sweet advice to take mental pictures of wedding high points
jokes.punchline: Jim immediately takes a mental picture, but 'Pam blinked' — treating the romantic moment with the mundane logic of an actual bad photo
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The structure is nearly perfect — the aunt's advice is genuinely sweet, Jim's immediate earnest attempt is charming, and then 'Oh, you blinked' subverts it with mundane camera logic. 'Should have hired a professional to take the mental pictures' is a great extension. It's funny AND reveals Jim's character beautifully — romantic but playful. Earns the 8+ score.

jokes.text: Dwight's seduction CD for Michael: 'Hello. My name is Dwight Schrute. If you're listening to this, you're a lucky woman Michael has seduced... Don't be scared of your night in heaven.'
jokes.setup: Dwight presents Michael with a mixtape to play for women he brings back to his hotel room
jokes.punchline: The mix is actually Dwight speaking on it — introducing himself and providing instructions as if narrating Michael's love life
jokes.explanation: This is among the episode's best jokes. The concept — Dwight recording a spoken-word intro for Michael's romantic encounters — is absurdly original. 'Don't be scared of your night in heaven' is a spectacular line. The idea that Dwight has pre-produced this, that he identified himself by full name, and that he considers this 'practical' — all of it is deeply, specifically Dwight. Highly quotable. Justifies 8+.

jokes.text: Hotel guest who reserved the honeymoon suite the night before says: 'Hey. Got the room the night before you guys. I'll break in the bed.'
jokes.setup: Jim and Pam check in and ask to see the honeymoon suite early
jokes.punchline: A stranger cheerfully announces he'll 'break in the bed' for them — obscene but delivered with total casualness
jokes.explanation: A quick cringe gag that lands — the cheerfulness of the delivery makes it funnier than it has any right to be. Low character integration since it's a one-off guest, but the economy is excellent.

jokes.text: Jim's reaction to the 'break in the bed' comment: 'I'm gonna need the name and cell phone number of the housekeeper responsible for changing the sheets, please.'
jokes.setup: A stranger has just said he'll 'break in' the honeymoon suite bed the night before Jim and Pam's wedding
jokes.punchline: Jim's response is hyper-specific, practical, and deeply revolted — going straight to logistics rather than objecting emotionally
jokes.explanation: Jim's typically Jim response — the horror is expressed through bureaucratic specificity rather than outrage. 'The housekeeper responsible for changing the sheets' is beautifully precise. Works as both character comedy and reaction beat.

jokes.text: Dwight's hotel reservation: Confirmation number 'Romeo, Tango, G, 7-7-4-5' and a pre-negotiated 'room with two safes'
jokes.setup: Michael has no reservation; Dwight checks in with military precision
jokes.punchline: Dwight's confirmation number is a military phonetic sequence and he's specifically requested TWO safes in his room
jokes.explanation: The room-with-two-safes detail is perfect Dwight paranoia. The military phonetic alphabet confirmation number suggests he specifically requested a code-worthy number. Strong character integration — these details are completely specific to Dwight Schrute's worldview.

jokes.text: Dwight's room-switch manipulation: He lies about the reservation being under 'M. Scott,' gets Michael excited, then reveals it was a 'test' — and Michael failed by being unwilling to share.
jokes.setup: Michael needs to stay in Dwight's room; Dwight initially refuses. Then a reservation under 'M. Scott' appears.
jokes.punchline: Dwight reveals the 'M. Scott' room was his all along — a loyalty test Michael failed by not offering to share when roles were reversed
jokes.explanation: A well-constructed bit. Dwight's strategic manipulation — engineering a fake-out loyalty test — is both absurd and perfectly in character. The structure is solid: setup (Michael needs room), misdirection (M. Scott reservation), reveal (it was a test). Dwight's 'dungeon wisdom test' escalation is a great button.

jokes.text: Michael's excuse for not sharing: 'If I have a woman up there and things are getting amorous, she's gonna get turned off if she looks in the bathroom and she sees you brushing your teeth with butter and clay.'
jokes.setup: Michael is trying to justify why Dwight can't stay in his room
jokes.punchline: He invents the specific detail of Dwight brushing teeth with 'butter and clay' as a dealbreaker for romance
jokes.explanation: 'Brushing your teeth with butter and clay' is a perfect absurdist detail — specific enough to be disturbing, weird enough to be hilarious, and not entirely implausible for Dwight Schrute. Strong specificity lifts this above average.

jokes.text: Dwight: 'You must pass the dungeon wisdom test. It worked. When Mary was denied a room at the inn, Jesus was born. When Michael was denied a room at the inn, we don't know what happens, because that story hasn't been told yet.'
jokes.setup: Dwight reveals his room-swap was a 'dungeon wisdom test' and draws a biblical parallel
jokes.punchline: He compares Michael being denied a hotel room to Mary and Joseph, then undercuts it with 'that story hasn't been told yet' — leaving Michael's destiny portentously open
jokes.explanation: The biblical parallel is inspired — comparing Michael's hotel room situation to the Nativity is absurd, and then the punchline ('we don't know what happens because that story hasn't been told yet') is genuinely clever. It treats Michael as a mythological figure whose narrative is still unfolding. High originality, great structure, and deeply Dwight in its portentousness. Earns 8+.

jokes.text: Stanley's reaction to Michael asking to share his queen bed: 'A queen-size bed is five feet wide. I am not five-feet wide, Michael.'
jokes.setup: Michael asks to share Stanley's hotel room. Stanley has one queen bed. Michael suggests they share it.
jokes.punchline: Stanley points out the mathematical absurdity while implicitly calling Michael fat — 'I am not five feet wide' reframes the insult as logistics
jokes.explanation: Stanley's deadpan dismissal is perfect. The line works because it's technically a complaint about Michael's weight dressed up as a geometry lesson. Classic Stanley — utterly done with everything.

jokes.text: Michael: 'A queen-size bed is five feet wide. I am not five-feet wide, Michael.' / Stanley: 'I'm not a physics major, Stanley. I'm just saying be careful.'
jokes.setup: Michael tries to argue that he and Stanley could share a queen bed
jokes.punchline: Michael addresses Stanley as 'Michael' and himself as 'Stanley' mid-argument — then deflects with 'I'm not a physics major'
jokes.explanation: The name-swap is a transcript artifact that may be a character confusion gag — Michael gets so flustered he swaps names. 'I'm not a physics major' as a non-sequitur defense against a geometry argument is classic Michael verbal escape. Competent but not a highlight.

jokes.text: Michael: 'I'm not a physics major, Stanley.' [in response to Stanley's math about the bed]
jokes.setup: Stanley is making a simple point about the bed being 5 feet wide
jokes.punchline: Michael deflects with 'I'm not a physics major' — misidentifying the relevant academic discipline (it's math/geometry, not physics)
jokes.explanation: Michael's clueless deflection — using the wrong science — is perfectly Michael. He wants to appear dismissive of 'technicalities' but reveals his ignorance. The wrong field of study is the joke, and it's specifically Michael's flavor of idiocy.

jokes.text: Michael asks Ryan and Kelly to share their room. Ryan: 'Oh, gross.' Kelly: 'Blow my brains out.'
jokes.setup: Michael continues his desperate room-search and approaches Ryan and Kelly
jokes.punchline: Both respond with graphic disgust — Kelly's 'Blow my brains out' being the more extreme of the two
jokes.explanation: Quick double-take reaction that works primarily through Kelly's escalation — 'blow my brains out' is more extreme than needed, which is funny. Fairly mechanical but efficient.

jokes.text: Toby offers Michael his extra twin bed, then adds: 'You are going to be sleeping by yourself for the rest of your life, so you should just get used to it.'
jokes.setup: Toby is the only one willing to help Michael, offering his spare bed
jokes.punchline: His offer is immediately followed by a brutally honest prediction about Michael's romantic future — delivered helpfully, as advice
jokes.explanation: This works on multiple levels: Toby is the only one kind enough to offer help, but his kindness comes with an accidental (or deliberate?) cruelty. The delivery as practical life advice makes it darker. Strong character integration — this is exactly how Toby's sad worldview manifests.

jokes.text: Jim's dad: Meemaw is 'the only 80-year-old with no smile wrinkles'
jokes.setup: The group is identifying Pam's grandmother at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: She's identifiable by the absence of smile lines — a physical marker of her humorless severity
jokes.explanation: A nicely observed character introduction joke. 'No smile wrinkles' efficiently tells us everything about Meemaw's personality. Good economy.

jokes.text: Michael to Jim and Pam: 'That is seriously going to impede my ability to hook up with your female relatives.' Then: 'Pretty sure everybody heard that. Didn't move my lips.'
jokes.setup: Jim and Pam ask Michael not to give a toast since it's blood relatives only
jokes.punchline: Michael's complaint is that not being allowed to speak will hurt his pickup chances — then attempts to claim he was ventriloquizing when everyone hears
jokes.explanation: 'Didn't move my lips' is a wonderful button — Michael's magical thinking that he can retroactively deny saying something out loud by claiming ventriloquism. The segue from hook-up strategy complaint to the denial is fast and funny. Strong Michael character work.

jokes.text: Meemaw to Pam: 'I wasn't sure about your branch of the family after I heard about your parents' divorce. But you and Jim are just perfect. God bless you.' Pam: 'Thank you. But nobody's perfect.' Meemaw: 'Well, I wouldn't care to live if I thought that.'
jokes.setup: Meemaw warmly compliments Pam and Jim as 'just perfect'
jokes.punchline: Pam's humble deflection ('nobody's perfect') prompts Meemaw to reveal she literally could not face existence if she believed imperfection was universal — a startlingly dark worldview from a sweet old lady
jokes.explanation: 'I wouldn't care to live if I thought that' is an unexpectedly dark and funny line from the prim grandmother. The structure works perfectly — Pam's attempt at humility inadvertently reveals Meemaw's rigid perfectionism, which borders on existential. Good misdirection from sweet to alarming.

jokes.text: Pam's father introduces his girlfriend Kristy, who is clearly very young. Jim's dad asks 'This your niece?' — Pam's dad: 'No, she's my girlfriend.'
jokes.setup: Pam's dad proudly introduces a young woman named Kristy to Jim's dad
jokes.punchline: The age gap is so apparent that Jim's dad assumes she must be a niece
jokes.explanation: A predictable age-gap joke but executed efficiently. The niece assumption is the obvious joke and the show leans into it without much additional spin. Functional but below average originality for this episode.

jokes.text: Dwight to Jim's young nephew: Explains at length why Jim is his boss despite Dwight being smarter — 'Because while I was busy trying to improve the company, Jim, the bad man, was busy kissing the boss man's butt.'
jokes.setup: A child asks Dwight why 'the bad man' (Jim) is his boss if Dwight is smarter
jokes.punchline: Dwight launches into a bitter, totally earnest explanation of office politics to a child, calling Jim 'the bad man' and himself a selfless company improver — confirming exactly how he sees himself
jokes.explanation: The child interlocutor is inspired — it forces Dwight to simplify his grievances into their most cartoon form ('the bad man'). His worldview expressed to a child reveals how genuinely childlike his own grudge is. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Pam introduces Kevin, but Kevin's sister-in-law Penny thought his name was 'Gill' — and she assumed he was Oscar's boyfriend. Oscar: 'You thought I was dating this?'
jokes.setup: Pam introduces Kevin and Oscar to her sister Penny
jokes.punchline: Penny mistook Kevin for Oscar's boyfriend; Oscar is more offended by the idea of dating Kevin than by the gay assumption
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's better structured jokes. The three-layer reveal is excellent: (1) wrong name, (2) assumed they were a couple, (3) Oscar's outrage is entirely about being matched with Kevin, not the gay assumption. 'You thought I was dating THIS?' — the emphasis on 'this' is devastating and quotable. Oscar's dignity being primarily about Kevin's undesirability is a sharp character insight.

jokes.text: Oscar: 'I'm not gay. I'm Kevin.' Then: 'Are you seeing anyone right now?' Oscar: 'She has a boyfriend. He's out of town.' 'Cool. Thank you.'
jokes.setup: Oscar has been deeply insulted by the assumption he's dating Kevin
jokes.punchline: Kevin immediately pivots to asking Penny out; Oscar volunteering that her boyfriend is 'out of town' is a bizarre wingman moment
jokes.explanation: The escalation from mutual mortification to Kevin immediately trying to date Penny is a good beat. Oscar oddly volunteering 'He's out of town' like a reluctant wingman is a character-specific weird detail. Good follow-through.

jokes.text: Meredith has switched place cards to sit at the young people's table; Dwight casually reveals he switched his card with Erin's to sit at the head table.
jokes.setup: Jim and Pam notice Meredith is at the wrong table
jokes.punchline: Dwight immediately reveals he also switched — to get himself to the head family table where he 'belongs'
jokes.explanation: A quick efficient joke — Meredith sneaking to the young people's table and Dwight sneaking to the head table are comic mirror images. Dwight's 'where I belong' is a nice character beat. Efficient but not exceptional.

jokes.text: Michael at the head table: 'Head table. Where I belong.' Jim: 'It's just for family.' Michael: 'I know.'
jokes.setup: Michael has positioned himself at the family head table at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: When told it's for family, Michael simply says 'I know' — implying he considers himself family, which he genuinely believes
jokes.explanation: Michael's delusion that he's family is expressed with perfect economy. 'I know' does all the work — his total sincerity makes this a good character beat rather than just an awkward moment.

jokes.text: Dwight identifies Isabel Poreba: 'In 1996, her 10th grade volleyball team went 10 and 2.'
jokes.setup: Dwight has researched all the female wedding guests; he identifies another target
jokes.punchline: His most specific intel on a romantic prospect is a 27-year-old volleyball statistic from her adolescence
jokes.explanation: A great callback to the Jocelyn joke. The specificity of '10th grade volleyball team went 10 and 2' as romantic due diligence is wonderfully absurd. Michael's confused 'What am I supposed to do with that?' is the perfect reaction. The '10 and 2' detail has a good record quality that Dwight adds with genuine pride.

jokes.text: Michael's wedding toast pickup strategy: 'right, so I'll be like, you're so sweet, guys, and so kind, and that's when I'll do the face like — like what? Right. And then we'll just give 'em a little punch to the back. A noogie.'
jokes.setup: Michael is strategizing how to attract women at the wedding
jokes.punchline: His seduction technique culminates in a noogie — a childhood hair-rub aggression move — which he considers romantic
jokes.explanation: Michael's 'noogie' as the climax of a seduction technique is a good absurdist beat. His earnestness about it is what sells it. The button 'Never got married... never... for a noogie' is a solid payoff.

jokes.text: Pam's brothers' toast talking head: 'They have hilarious material and they are going to totally deliver it wrong. I would kill with the brother stuff. It should be me up there.'
jokes.setup: Pam's brothers are preparing to give toasts at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: Andy considers their material his by right and is confident he would do it better — an absurd professional jealousy of someone else's family stories
jokes.explanation: Andy's performative confidence about 'the brother stuff' is a good character beat. His sense of comedy entitlement — feeling robbed of a toast opportunity at someone else's sister's wedding — is specific to Andy's particular narcissism.

jokes.text: Pam's brothers' toast about Pam: 'Pam, you've got the greatest smile, and your body is really fine. Smoking.'
jokes.setup: Pam's brothers give what appears to be a heartfelt toast at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: It pivots from 'greatest smile' to 'your body is really fine. Smoking.' — an objectifying compliment delivered by her brothers at her rehearsal dinner
jokes.explanation: The brothers' toast going immediately to 'smoking' about their sister is good cringe comedy. The added detail that Michael thinks this will inspire wives to 'kick it up a notch' with 'a little mo' cardio' adds another uncomfortable layer.

jokes.text: Michael's 'freestanding comedy' toast: begins with 'What is the deal with the smart car?' doing a Seinfeld impression, including 'I drive a smart car' and concluding that KITT from Knight Rider and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang are smarter cars
jokes.setup: Michael promised not to give a toast, so he announces he'll do 'freestanding comedy' instead
jokes.punchline: His 'comedy' is a Seinfeld-style 'what's the deal' bit that goes nowhere, culminating in preferring fictional talking cars over smart cars as proof of intelligence
jokes.explanation: Michael doing bad stand-up at a wedding rehearsal dinner is inspired. The 'what is the deal' Seinfeld homage is perfectly bad comedy — the logic of KITT and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang as 'smart' cars for talking is committed absurdist reasoning. His 'everybody can laugh, not just the idiots' is a great condescending aside. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Andy responds to Pete's toast with 'Douche. Ah, thanks, Pete. That was really nice.'
jokes.setup: Pete gives a toast for Jim and Pam
jokes.punchline: Andy mutters 'douche' under his breath then immediately pivots to fake-sincere appreciation
jokes.explanation: Quick Andy character beat. The whiplash from insult to fake sincerity is his particular brand of repressed jealousy. Functional but not exceptional.

jokes.text: Jim's rehearsal dinner toast: confesses he knows how to make a photocopy and that teaching him to drive stick 'took a year' — Pam: 'I've been driving stick since high school.' Jim: 'Very nice.'
jokes.setup: Jim gives a romantic toast admitting he used excuses to spend time with Pam
jokes.punchline: Pam deflates his romantic confessions one by one — she knew he could photocopy, and reveals she's been driving stick since high school
jokes.explanation: Beautifully constructed romantic comedy beat. Jim's confession of his pretextual helplessness is sweet, and Pam casually puncturing each excuse with 'I've been driving stick since high school' shows their perfect dynamic — she knew all along. 'Very nice' as Jim's accepting response is perfect. Earns its score through genuine heart mixed with comedy.

jokes.text: Jim's toast accidentally reveals Pam's pregnancy: 'if you'd all raise your glasses — not Pam, for obvious reasons.' 'What's obvious?' 'Why can't Pam drink?'
jokes.setup: Jim gives a beautiful, heartfelt toast and invites everyone to raise their glasses
jokes.punchline: He reflexively excludes Pam from drinking 'for obvious reasons' — immediately alerting the guests that something is up
jokes.explanation: A beautifully constructed cringe moment. The romantic buildup makes the accidental reveal hit harder. 'For obvious reasons' is exactly the kind of thing Jim would say without thinking — and it's a great structural joke because the audience sees it coming a split second before the guests react. The ripple effect of the room questioning it is well-executed escalation.

jokes.text: Jim's attempted cover: 'She can do whatever she wants. Though she shouldn't. She shouldn't, because she's an alcoholic. Pam is an alcoholic. That's not true.'
jokes.setup: Jim is trying to cover for accidentally revealing Pam is pregnant
jokes.punchline: His cover attempt pivots to calling Pam an alcoholic — which he immediately retracts — making things exponentially worse
jokes.explanation: Excellent escalation of the previous joke. Jim's panicked logic — pivoting to 'she's an alcoholic' as a cover story — is both very funny and very Jim. The self-correction ('That's not true') while the crowd processes it is perfectly timed. Each sentence makes things demonstrably worse. Strong structure.

jokes.text: Michael's rescue speech: 'They had an accident, and you know what? These two people, they're living together. They are having lots of consensual sex.'
jokes.setup: Jim has made things worse by calling Pam an alcoholic; Michael jumps in to 'help'
jokes.punchline: Michael's rescue focuses on announcing the couple has 'lots of consensual sex' to a room that includes Pam's grandmother
jokes.explanation: Michael jumping in to 'help' and immediately making it about consensual sex is perfect Michael Scott. The word 'consensual' — which he chooses as a reassurance but which implies the need for reassurance — is a great detail. 'They were living together — yes!' is him getting excited about his own non-disclosure.

jokes.text: Michael continues: 'And you know what? You can't expect them to be careful every time, because, frankly, it's just a different sensation... it's not necessarily different for the woman, but it is different—'
jokes.setup: Michael is trying to justify why Jim and Pam got pregnant, addressing the room including Meemaw
jokes.punchline: His explanation devolves into an enthusiastic defense of unprotected sex as a 'different sensation' to Pam's grandmother at her granddaughter's rehearsal dinner
jokes.explanation: The escalation of Michael's speech into explicitly discussing contraception-free sensation to an elderly conservative grandmother is peak cringe-Michael. The repeated attempts to stop him ('Michael. Stop.') that he overrides add to the horror. Strong character integration — only Michael would think this was helpful.

jokes.text: Michael's parting shot: 'My point is, I said what I wanted to say, and, Meemaw, I hope you heard every word.'
jokes.setup: Michael has been stopped mid-speech about unprotected sex at the rehearsal dinner
jokes.punchline: He signs off as if he's delivered a profound message — specifically addressing Meemaw to make sure she absorbed his sex-ed lecture
jokes.explanation: The button to the whole Michael speech sequence. His satisfaction at having delivered his message — and his specific desire that Meemaw heard it — is perfectly in character. His self-congratulatory obliviousness is the comedy engine here.

jokes.text: Meemaw talking head: 'I should have known. The hotel's television set had a movie on called Bruno last night. The remote control had so darn many buttons on it, I couldn't turn it off. So I had to just sit there while it happened to me.'
jokes.setup: Meemaw is clearly rattled by the evening's events — establishing her as very conservative
jokes.punchline: She reveals she was forced to watch the Sacha Baron Cohen film Bruno (2009, extremely graphic) because she couldn't figure out the remote — framing it as a violation she endured passively
jokes.explanation: This is one of the episode's best jokes. The specificity of Bruno (2009) — one of the most aggressively sexual, graphic films possible — being what the conservative grandmother watched on loop because she couldn't work the remote is inspired. 'So I had to just sit there while it happened to me' is a devastating line — the passive victimhood framing of watching a film. High originality, perfect economy, strong character. Earns 8+.

jokes.text: Jim: 'I think it was a little touch and go at first, but we saved it, I believe.' Pam: 'I can't believe it was me.' Jim: 'I know. I can't believe it was you, either.' Jim: 'I actually think it takes a lot of pressure off of me.'
jokes.setup: Jim and Pam debrief after the rehearsal dinner disaster — Jim accidentally revealed the pregnancy
jokes.punchline: Jim is relieved that Pam is now the one who screwed up — 'takes a lot of pressure off me' — as if they have a quota for embarrassing moments
jokes.explanation: A warm, character-driven beat. Jim's relief that the pressure is off him lands as both affectionate and self-aware. Good but not exceptional — relies on the goodwill built in the scene rather than strong construction.

jokes.text: Pam: 'Is there something about being a manager that makes you say stupid things?' Jim: 'I have not found that to be the case.'
jokes.setup: Pam is mortified that Jim's toast revealed her pregnancy
jokes.punchline: Jim's deadpan 'I have not found that to be the case' — implying he's been a manager without similar disasters — is technically true while being a studied non-answer
jokes.explanation: Jim's formal denial is a nice quick beat. The bureaucratic phrasing ('I have not found that to be the case') for what should be a personal response is appropriately Jim. Good economy.

jokes.text: Michael: 'Can you believe it? He screwed up, not me.' [giddy at Jim's mistake]
jokes.setup: The rehearsal dinner disaster has just concluded
jokes.punchline: Michael is genuinely delighted that Jim — not he — caused the catastrophe, which is his benchmark for success
jokes.explanation: Quick Michael moment that's good but unremarkable. His definition of personal success as 'not being the worst person in the room' is established characterization played well here.

jokes.text: Andy: 'Meemaw's not coming to the wedding. She's leaving tomorrow morning.' Michael: 'Oh my god. Are you serious?' Dwight: 'There's gonna be a free room?'
jokes.setup: The group learns Meemaw has been so scandalized she's leaving before the wedding
jokes.punchline: Dwight's only concern is the freed-up hotel room — his priorities are perfectly misaligned with the emotional reality
jokes.explanation: Dwight's 'There's gonna be a free room?' is a perfect character beat — the fastest possible demonstration of his priorities. His roomlessness earlier in the episode makes this a satisfying callback. Strong economy (five words), peak Dwight.

jokes.text: Meemaw on the phone: 'Oh, you're that foul man that kept talking about intercourse.'
jokes.setup: Michael calls Meemaw to make amends
jokes.punchline: Meemaw's summary of Michael — 'that foul man that kept talking about intercourse' — is both accurate and hilarious as a character description
jokes.explanation: Meemaw's vocabulary ('foul man,' 'intercourse') perfectly captures her generation and worldview, and her reduction of Michael to this single defining characteristic is both fair and funny. A great callback line.

jokes.text: Michael's talking head: 'I'm actually great with old women. In fact, for the longest time, my best friend was my grandmother. And then she met Harriet, and now she thinks she's better than everybody.'
jokes.setup: Michael claims he can help with Meemaw because he's 'great with old women'
jokes.punchline: He reveals his grandmother abandoned him as her best friend for a new friend named Harriet — treating elderly social rejection as a genuine wound
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best Michael moments. The reveal that his 'best friend' was his grandmother, and his sense of betrayal when she made a new friend, is both deeply funny and genuinely revealing of his abandonment issues. 'And now she thinks she's better than everybody' — the resentment toward an elderly woman for having other friends — is a perfectly calibrated dark comedy line. High originality, strong structure, irreplaceably Michael. Earns 8+.

jokes.text: Michael tries to get Meemaw to 'chill out' about Pam's pregnancy: 'It's not 1890 anymore. It's modern day. And women have sex before marriage. And I think we need to celebrate that.'
jokes.setup: Michael is attempting to smooth things over with the offended conservative grandmother
jokes.punchline: His 'modern' argument frames pre-marital sex as a social achievement to 'celebrate' — to Pam's grandmother
jokes.explanation: More Michael diplomacy in Meemaw's room. The 'I think we need to celebrate that' framing as his diplomatic opening is characteristically counterproductive. Good character integration, though slightly below the earlier Meemaw-rescue attempts.

jokes.text: Michael to Meemaw: 'And I know in your day she would be considered a whore, but now women go out and they have sex and they get wild and they take their tops off and they have pictures taken of them. And we need to encourage that.'
jokes.setup: Michael is trying to be diplomatic with Meemaw about Pam's pre-marital pregnancy
jokes.punchline: His argument escalates from defending pre-marital sex to encouraging women to take their tops off for photos — as progressive values
jokes.explanation: The escalation from defending pre-marital pregnancy to 'they take their tops off and have pictures taken' as Michael's vision of female empowerment is wonderfully terrible. Only Michael Scott would genuinely believe this is a persuasive pro-women argument to a conservative grandmother. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Meemaw: 'People are like cats and dogs these days.' Michael: 'Exactly.' Meemaw: 'This used to be such a great country.' Michael: 'I know. I don't know what happened to it.'
jokes.setup: Michael has just finished making an impassioned defense of women taking their tops off
jokes.punchline: Meemaw's 'people are like cats and dogs' is a lament — but Michael enthusiastically agrees, having entirely missed the irony; they accidentally find common ground through mutual incomprehension
jokes.explanation: A beautifully observed beat — Michael accidentally agreeing with Meemaw's conservative lament while they're coming from diametrically opposed positions. 'I don't know what happened to it' from Michael after defending sex positivity is perfect dramatic irony.

jokes.text: Michael tells Meemaw they're naming the baby after her — 'Meemaw.' Meemaw: 'You mean Sylvia.' Michael: 'Yes. And if it's a boy, they will call it Sylvio.'
jokes.setup: Michael is trying to charm Meemaw into staying for the wedding
jokes.punchline: He invents the name 'Sylvio' for a potential boy as the natural masculine form of Sylvia — confident in a name he just made up
jokes.explanation: Michael's confident invention of 'Sylvio' as a boy's name and his certainty about it is good quick Michael characterization. The lie is transparent but he commits to it fully.

jokes.text: Michael's hotel party announcement: 'Par-tay. Room 639. Chicks are gonna be off the hook. Guys too, Oscar. Like Calvin Klein models.'
jokes.setup: Michael announces his hotel room party
jokes.punchline: He adds 'Guys too, Oscar. Like Calvin Klein models.' — a semi-aware nod to Oscar's sexuality delivered as an afterthought
jokes.explanation: Mild Michael moment — his attempt at inclusive party promotion is well-meaning but slightly awkward. The CK models detail is specific but the joke doesn't quite land strongly.

jokes.text: Kevin talking head: 'No one from the office has been to a real beer throw-down. If I was a girl, I would seriously reconsider coming to this party. But don't tell them that I said that, 'cause I want them there.'
jokes.setup: Michael has announced a wild hotel party
jokes.punchline: Kevin warns women (in a talking head addressed only to the camera) to reconsider attending, while simultaneously wanting them there — a complete absence of self-awareness about his own warning
jokes.explanation: A really good Kevin bit. The structure is excellent — the warning to women, the immediate retraction to keep them coming, and the absence of any recognition that this is contradictory. 'If I was a girl, I would seriously reconsider' is a genuine red-flag assessment from Kevin about his own friend group. Nicely dark.

jokes.text: Dwight's hotel bar outfit described as looking like he's 'going to a fish fry.' Dwight's explanation: 'No, they're howling at the moon. It's suggestive to women. Because of howling during sex.'
jokes.setup: Michael and Oscar critique Dwight's casual outfit for the hotel bar
jokes.punchline: Dwight reveals his wolves-howling-at-moon shirt is a deliberate seduction tool based on the theory that women associate howling with sexual behavior
jokes.explanation: The howling-during-sex seduction theory is wonderfully specific and completely Dwight. The pseudo-logical chain (shirt features howling → women think of sex howling → attraction) is absurdist in exactly Dwight's style. 'Because of howling during sex' delivered deadpan is very quotable.

jokes.text: Oscar: 'There's no such thing as a good hairpiece.' Michael: 'Yeah, but that's easy enough for you to say, Oscar. You have that thick, beautiful, Chicano hair. So nice.'
jokes.setup: The group discusses Kevin's toupee in the hotel bar
jokes.punchline: Michael defends Kevin's hairpiece by complimenting Oscar's natural hair — specifically calling it 'Chicano hair' with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: Michael's oblivious ethnic reference ('Chicano hair') is a mid-level Michael cringe beat — not his most inspired but characteristic of his well-meaning cluelessness.

jokes.text: Dwight worrying about Mose having to geld horses alone. Michael: 'Dwight, shut up about the farm. It's not relatable. Nobody owns a farm.' Isabel: 'Wait, you're worried about your horses? That's cool. How many horses do you have?'
jokes.setup: Michael tells Dwight to stop talking about his farm because it's 'not relatable'
jokes.punchline: Isabel — the woman Dwight is supposedly trying to impress — is actually charmed by the horse conversation Michael just killed
jokes.explanation: Good structural irony — Michael shuts down Dwight's best material right before the woman he's trying to impress expresses genuine interest in it. The comedic reversal is cleanly executed.

jokes.text: Dwight: 'Nine and three quarters.' [horses he owns]
jokes.setup: Isabel asks how many horses Dwight has
jokes.punchline: 'Nine and three quarters' — implying one horse is partially owned, or partially a horse, delivered with total matter-of-factness
jokes.explanation: Near-perfect answer. The fractional horse ownership delivered as a straight fact is one of the tightest jokes in the episode. Its economy is exceptional — three words do all the work. We don't know if it's a three-legged horse, a co-ownership situation, or something darker, and the ambiguity is the joke. Deeply Dwight — he would track horse ownership to the quarter. Earns 8+.

jokes.text: Dwight's 'Burger on the Go' invention: extracts six burgers or 12 sliders from a horse 'without killing the animal.' Then: 'George Foreman is still considering it. Sharp Image is still considering it. Skymall's still considering it. Hammacher Schlemmer's still considering it. Sears said no.'
jokes.setup: Dwight is explaining his farming ingenuity and inventions to Isabel
jokes.punchline: He has pitched a horse-burger extraction device to multiple retailers — all of whom are 'still considering it,' except Sears which definitively said no
jokes.explanation: This is among the episode's very best jokes. The concept of 'Burger on the Go' — horse-meat harvesting without killing the animal — is grotesque and absurd. The list of retailers he's pitched is a perfect escalation structure, with 'Sears said no' as a devastating button. Sears saying no (not the others, just Sears) is the most specific possible detail. The commitment to the list — naming each retailer — builds and builds. Exceptional originality, structure, and character integration. Earns 8+ decisively.

jokes.text: Michael: 'Toy Story, Finding Nemo, Up — I bawled the entire time. I cannot watch Pixar.' Jim and Pam try to stop him: 'Drop this one. Abort.' Michael: 'Why?' Jim: 'I found twins.'
jokes.setup: Michael is confessing emotional vulnerability at Pixar movies to the hotel bar group
jokes.punchline: Jim's only reason to shut Michael down is spotting male twins — his urgency about the twins completely upstages Michael's emotional admission
jokes.explanation: A good misdirection — Michael's Pixar confession being aborted for the twins sighting is funny, and then the twist that the twins are male (Michael was expecting female twins as pickup targets) is the secondary punchline.

jokes.text: Michael: 'Aren't they magnificent?' [about male twins] Dwight: 'They're men, Dwight.' Michael: 'I love finding a good set of twins.' Dwight: 'Something's wrong with you.'
jokes.setup: Michael has spotted the male twins and is gazing at them admiringly
jokes.punchline: Michael's 'Aren't they magnificent?' is replied to by himself (confused attribution in transcript — Dwight says 'They're men'), and he defends his twin fascination as an aesthetic appreciation
jokes.explanation: Decent Michael beat. His appreciating male twins without self-consciousness is a good character note, and Dwight's sober 'Something's wrong with you' functions as a straight-man line which is a role reversal.

jokes.text: Meredith dancing wildly at the hotel bar — others: 'Yeah, Meredith! Nice moves!' 'You call that a robot? Try being more robotic, okay? Like this.'
jokes.setup: The hotel bar has become a dance floor; Meredith is enthusiastically dancing
jokes.punchline: Michael and Andy critique and one-up her dancing, leading to competitive dance floor escalation
jokes.explanation: Physical comedy that plays better as a visual. The transcript loses most of the humor here. Meredith dancing wildly is an expected character beat; the robot challenge is a mild comedic escalation.

jokes.text: Andy does a split on the dance floor and screams — then: 'I was dancing and I did a split and I landed on my car keys in my pocket. I tore my scrotum. I need you to take me to the hospital.'
jokes.setup: Andy is enthusiastically dancing and one-upping Michael on the dance floor
jokes.punchline: He tears his scrotum on his car keys doing a split — the injury is both grotesque and perfectly logical
jokes.explanation: Andy injuring his scrotum on his own car keys is a well-constructed physical comedy premise. The escalation from competitive dancing to genuine medical emergency is fast and effective. 'I tore my scrotum' delivered to Pam the night before her wedding is a great cringe beat. The car-key specificity is what elevates it above generic physical comedy.

jokes.text: Andy: 'Andy, I'm getting married in eight hours.' Andy: 'Everyone else is too drunk.' Andy: 'Just don't let me die here.'
jokes.setup: Andy needs hospital transport for his scrotum injury
jokes.punchline: His final appeal — 'Just don't let me die here' — is both genuinely pathetic and comically disproportionate to the actual injury
jokes.explanation: A good escalation of the previous Andy beat — 'Just don't let me die here' adds the right amount of melodrama to a groin injury. The timing of Pam being called away from wedding prep for this is the cringe engine.

jokes.text: Jim learns Pam is taking Andy to the hospital: 'He tore his scrotum dancing.' Jim: 'What?' Pam: 'Is in my room, icing his balls.' Jim: 'What?' Pam: 'Please stop saying what.'
jokes.setup: Pam calls Jim to explain why she's taking Andy to the hospital
jokes.punchline: Jim's increasingly incredulous 'What?' responses to each new detail, until Pam tells him to stop
jokes.explanation: A solid escalation beat. Three 'whats' in a row, each one warranted, until Pam shuts it down. 'Icing his balls' as a matter-of-fact update delivered by Pam to her fiancé the night before their wedding has good cringe energy.

jokes.text: Jim's bar companions mock him: 'It's after midnight. You're married. He's married!' Jim: 'Oh, that's not how that works.'
jokes.setup: It's just past midnight, and Michael and Dwight tease Jim about technically being married now
jokes.punchline: Michael and Dwight apply their own rules about midnight marriage while Jim protests
jokes.explanation: A mild joke — the 'midnight married' superstition isn't a real thing, which is part of the joke, but the comedic payoff is thin.

jokes.text: Michael imitates Pam as a nagging wife: 'Jim, take the baby to the zoo, 'cause I want to sit at home and eat bonbons and clip my toenails... Jim, hey, why don't you braid my hair? I want to watch TV.' Jim: 'Now you sound like Kermit.'
jokes.setup: Michael is teasing Jim about married life
jokes.punchline: Michael's impression of Pam as a demanding wife reaches a register where Jim compares him to Kermit the Frog
jokes.explanation: The Kermit comparison is a good button — Michael's voice impression apparently goes full Muppet. The nagging wife material is fairly generic but the Kermit reveal saves it.

jokes.text: Pam driving Andy to the hospital: 'Well, at least slow down a little bit, because every little bump in the road is major pain on... my scrotum.'
jokes.setup: Pam is driving Andy to the hospital late at night before her wedding
jokes.punchline: Andy's request to slow down reveals every pothole is agonizing for his injury — the scrotum reiteration is the punchline
jokes.explanation: The running Andy scrotum gag maintained. The pause before 'my scrotum' lands as expected — a reliable if not inspired beat at this point in the escalation.

jokes.text: Andy: 'Well, it's also to make sure that we have a great time at your stupid wedding, so...' [justifying his dance injury as 'doing Pam's job']
jokes.setup: Pam says her job the night before her wedding is just to get married. Andy argues he was 'doing her job' by entertaining everyone.
jokes.punchline: Andy frames tearing his scrotum as professional service to Pam — he was 'doing her job' of ensuring wedding fun
jokes.explanation: Andy's logic here — that entertaining at Pam's wedding was 'her job' that he took on by splitting — is self-serving delusion typical of his character. The wounded dignity is well-played.

jokes.text: Jim talking head: 'I just spent the night with the bride the night before the wedding. Oh yeah. She stepped on my hand on her way to the bathroom, so...'
jokes.setup: Jim references spending the night before the wedding with Pam
jokes.punchline: The 'wild night' with the bride amounts to her stepping on his hand going to the bathroom
jokes.explanation: Jim's deadpan 'night with the bride' reveal being her stepping on him is good subversion of honeymoon expectations. 'So...' as the trailing button is classic Jim-to-camera. Good economy.

jokes.text: Jim: 'Andy, did I dream that you were crying through the night?' Andy: 'No. No, that was real.'
jokes.setup: Jim wakes up in the hotel room he ended up sharing with Andy
jokes.punchline: Andy crying all night through his scrotum pain was real, confirmed matter-of-factly
jokes.explanation: A great morning-after beat. Jim hoping it was a dream; Andy's flat 'No. No, that was real.' is perfectly delivered (implied). The idea that Jim spent his pre-wedding night listening to Andy cry is a good payoff to the whole scrotum subplot.

jokes.text: Kevin's shoes were destroyed overnight by the hotel. Hotel manager: 'When the bag was opened by our shoeshine, the smell overcame him. I, too, smelled them and made the choice that they must be thrown away.' Kevin: 'But that was my only pair of shoes.' Manager: 'It became a safety issue, sir.'
jokes.setup: Kevin left his shoes to be shined overnight; they haven't been returned
jokes.punchline: The hotel has incinerated Kevin's shoes because the smell was so severe it 'overcame' the shoeshine person and the manager — classified as a safety issue
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best background gags. The hotel's professional reaction to Kevin's shoes — the shoeshine being 'overcome,' the manager personally verifying and agreeing on destruction, the safety classification, the incineration — is a beautiful escalating bit. 'It became a safety issue, sir' is an exceptional line. Kevin's plaintive 'But that was my only pair of shoes' adds the perfect sad note. Earns 8+.

jokes.text: Dwight talking head morning after: Michael ate 'a whole bunch of sunflower seeds' after Dwight fell asleep — but then: 'I wouldn't want to take you away from Pam on the morning of her wedding. She needs you, Isabel.'
jokes.setup: Morning-after scene in Dwight's room — Isabel is there
jokes.punchline: Dwight being unexpectedly considerate to Isabel, referencing Pam — revealing they spent the night together while maintaining plausible deniability about what that means
jokes.explanation: A sweet misdirection — Dwight's consideration for Pam through Isabel reframes him briefly as considerate. The sunflower seeds detail (Michael eating them after Dwight slept) is a good background absurdist detail.

jokes.text: Michael is jealous/probing about Dwight's hookup: 'She made love like a tiger.' Michael: 'Bride side or groom side? Or townie?' Dwight: 'She was from Europe.' Michael: 'Bet she had hairy armpits.' Dwight: 'No.'
jokes.setup: Michael interrogates Dwight about his successful hookup
jokes.punchline: Michael's European assumption goes straight to armpit hair; Dwight's flat 'No' is the button
jokes.explanation: 'She made love like a tiger' and Michael's immediate armpit-hair assumption about Europeans are good. The taxonomy of 'bride side, groom side, or townie' for categorizing hookup origins is a nice Dwight detail.

jokes.text: Dwight dismisses Isabel as 'a dental hygienist from Carbondale': 'You have to take X-rays. You have to scrape the plaque off people's teeth. You have to tell kids when to spit and make sure that they're not scared when the dentist comes in.' Then: 'I already have a European girlfriend.'
jokes.setup: Michael suggests Dwight should pursue Isabel; Dwight explains why she's beneath him
jokes.punchline: His dismissal of dental hygiene as beneath him is specific and absurd; then he reveals he has 'a European girlfriend' — the woman he just met and slept with — as if she's now a committed relationship
jokes.explanation: The dental hygienist rant — listing the specific tasks of the job as if they're demeaning — is great absurdist snobbery. But the real payoff is 'I already have a European girlfriend' — Dwight has mentally locked in the woman he met last night as a relationship, while also dismissing Isabel for being too common. Excellent character integration.

jokes.text: Angela and Oscar have clearly spent time together — Oscar is nursing what appears to be morning-after distress; Angela says wedding emotions made her cry. Oscar: 'People say you cry all the time.' Angela: 'Well, that's...' [trails off]
jokes.setup: Oscar and Angela appear to have spent the night talking/consoling each other
jokes.punchline: Oscar reveals people say she cries 'all the time,' which she can't dispute — the shared vulnerability between two characters who are usually guarded/prickly
jokes.explanation: A quietly funny beat that works primarily through character irony — Angela who brands herself as unsentimental being known as someone who cries all the time. Subtle.

jokes.text: Andy and Kevin morning-after exchange about the scrotum injury: Kevin: 'There's still something there?' Andy: 'Excuse me?' Kevin: 'It didn't get torn off?' Andy: 'No they didn't— nothing got torn off. Who told you that?' Kevin: 'I may have told some people that.'
jokes.setup: Kevin is checking in on Andy's scrotum injury the morning of the wedding
jokes.punchline: Kevin has apparently told people Andy's scrotum was 'torn off' — having spread a dramatic exaggeration through the wedding party
jokes.explanation: Kevin's earnest question about whether Andy's anatomy is still intact — and the reveal that he's been spreading the rumor that it was 'torn off' — is a great escalation. 'I may have told some people that' is perfectly Kevin-calibrated: mild guilt, zero remorse. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Michael offers Andy his seat cushion: 'I was thinking the wood might be too hard on your damaged penis. Make it softer.' Andy: 'It's my scrotum.' Michael: 'Um. And it was. Thank you.'
jokes.setup: Michael is being unusually considerate about Andy's injury
jokes.punchline: He misidentifies the anatomy ('damaged penis'), is corrected, then accepts the correction and confirms the seat was indeed for the scrotum — 'And it was. Thank you.'
jokes.explanation: 'And it was. Thank you.' is the best line in this exchange — Michael processing the anatomical correction with such measured acceptance is very funny. The beat is brief but well-executed.

jokes.text: Michael confesses: 'I may have told some people that.' (that Andy's genitals were torn off)
jokes.setup: Andy demands to know who spread the rumor that his genitalia was torn off
jokes.punchline: Michael casually admits responsibility, completely unbothered by the medical misinformation he's spread
jokes.explanation: The casual confession — 'I may have told some people that' — delivered with Michael's signature blend of sheepishness and total lack of remorse is excellent. Economy is strong: five words that reveal everything about Michael's relationship with truth.

jokes.text: Michael's wedding gift: a painted portrait of Jim and Pam from memory — 'And I have another one of them in the nude. But that one is for me.'
jokes.setup: Michael reveals his unique wedding gift: a painted portrait from memory
jokes.punchline: He also painted a nude version which he is keeping for himself
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. The setup (portrait from memory) is already good; the reveal of a nude version kept for himself is perfectly calibrated — it's creepy, possessive, and completely Michael. 'But that one is for me' delivered as a perfectly natural aside is the killer. Maximum economy (five words for the punchline), perfect character integration, high originality. One of the most quotable moments in the episode. Earns 8.5.

jokes.text: Oscar/Kevin's wedding gift: 'I got them a set of turtle-grilling pots, shell hammer, and bibs.'
jokes.setup: Guests are discussing/revealing their wedding gifts
jokes.punchline: Kevin's gift is a turtle-cooking kit — an extremely specific and unusual culinary gift for a wedding
jokes.explanation: The specificity of turtle-grilling equipment as a wedding gift is a good Kevin absurdist beat. 'Shell hammer and bibs' adds great detail. Solid.

jokes.text: Pam's dress: 'Is it zipping over your belly? Don't squish the baby.' Pam: 'Thank you, weirdo.'
jokes.setup: Pam is getting into her wedding dress while visibly pregnant
jokes.punchline: Someone's helpfully alarmed advice to 'not squish the baby' is simultaneously practical and cringe-inducing
jokes.explanation: Mild pre-wedding cringe. 'Thank you, weirdo' is a good reaction. Nothing remarkable.

jokes.text: Everybody noticing and commenting on Pam's dad's young girlfriend's 'stupid blond extensions. It's like they were made from a plastic broom.'
jokes.setup: The women getting ready notice Kristy (Pam's dad's young girlfriend) in the room
jokes.punchline: Her hair extensions are compared to a plastic broom — a specific and unflattering image
jokes.explanation: A mildly funny specific insult about the hair extensions. The 'plastic broom' image is vivid but the joke is relatively cheap — an appearance jab without much comedy architecture.

jokes.text: Pam's mom upon seeing her: 'Oh darling, you look beautiful.' Then immediately: 'I hope he deserves you.' Then: 'Remember, you don't have to do this. You don't.'
jokes.setup: Pam's mom sees her in her wedding dress on the wedding day
jokes.punchline: The escalating sabotage: compliment → doubt about Jim's worthiness → 'you don't have to do this' — increasing panic from Pam's projecting post-divorce mother
jokes.explanation: A good escalating cringe beat. The mother's post-divorce projection manifesting as pre-wedding cold feet encouragement is character-consistent and effective. Pam shutting her down ('totally projecting and being a drag') is a good reaction.

jokes.text: Jim's pre-wedding visit to Pam: 'Is this allowed?' Pam: 'No, no. But I'm allowing it. Just come here.' Jim: 'That was an intelligent comment.'
jokes.setup: Jim sneaks to see Pam before the wedding despite tradition
jokes.punchline: Pam overrules wedding tradition with 'I'm allowing it' — authority granted to herself — and Jim's 'that was an intelligent comment' is dry acknowledgment of her casual self-authorization
jokes.explanation: A warm Jim-and-Pam moment with a light comedy beat. Jim's 'that was an intelligent comment' is dry praise for Pam's self-granted authority. Good but not exceptional — mostly serving the emotional arc.

jokes.text: Pam's confessional: 'Hello, stranger. How do I look?' Dwight: 'Oh. Fine. Abel, nice to see you.' Pam: 'What do you want?' Dwight: 'Um, nothing... Anymore.'
jokes.setup: Pam, in her wedding dress, asks Dwight how she looks
jokes.punchline: Dwight initially can't look at her directly ('Fine. Abel, nice to see you') — clearly moved — then says 'nothing... anymore' implying he once wanted something he now accepts he can't have
jokes.explanation: A surprisingly poignant Dwight moment that's also genuinely funny. 'Fine. Abel, nice to see you' — addressing an invisible 'Abel' to avoid looking at Pam — is an absurd avoidance tactic. 'Nothing... anymore.' lands emotionally and comically: it implies Dwight had feelings/intentions that he's now formally retiring. The ellipsis does real work. Strong character integration for both characters.

jokes.text: Pam's veil has torn. She's upset. Jim secretly tears his tie to match: 'There. Now we're even.'
jokes.setup: Pam is upset that her veil tore — the 'one thing she was supposed to be able to control'
jokes.punchline: Jim tears his own tie to match her, equalizing their imperfection as a partnership
jokes.explanation: This is the episode's most emotionally resonant joke — it functions simultaneously as a romantic gesture and a comedic bit. 'There. Now we're even.' is perfection: three words that are both funny and deeply characterful. Jim's solution to Pam's distress being to make himself equally imperfect rather than fix hers is completely Jim Halpert. Economy is flawless, character integration is as high as it gets in this episode. Earns 8.5 for being the rare joke that makes you laugh and feel something.

jokes.text: Pam talking head: 'Everyone's driving me crazy. I know way too much about Andy's scrotum, and my mom won't stop freaking out about my dad's new girlfriend.'
jokes.setup: Pam reflects on the wedding morning chaos
jokes.punchline: Her list of grievances is led by Andy's scrotum knowledge — placing it before even her parents' drama as the top stressor
jokes.explanation: A good callback that also functions as a character beat — Pam's exasperated accounting of her wedding chaos, with Andy's scrotum leading the list, is both funny and sympathetic. Good economy.

jokes.text: Toby talking head: explains he's 'trying to decide if I have time to pee.' Oscar: 'How long do you take to pee?' Toby: 'The peeing is fast, Oscar. It's getting my tie back on.'
jokes.setup: Pre-ceremony chaos — everyone is scrambling to be ready
jokes.punchline: Toby's real bottleneck isn't biological but sartorial — the tie is the obstacle, not the urination
jokes.explanation: 'The peeing is fast, Oscar. It's getting my tie back on.' is a perfectly Toby line — overly specific, slightly pitiful, completely self-aware of his own minor incompetence. Strong character integration.

jokes.text: Michael in the hallway asks a woman if she has a snack in her purse — 'You're a mom. I just figured you might have—' She produces a Fruit Roll-Up. Michael: 'Do you have any of the very berry or ocean splash, or—?' Woman: 'No.' Michael: 'Oh. Okay. Were you saving it?'
jokes.setup: Michael is wandering the pre-ceremony hallway and asks a stranger for food
jokes.punchline: He accepts the apricot Fruit Roll-Up but immediately asks if she has better flavors, and then whether she was 'saving it' when she says no
jokes.explanation: Great Michael moment. The specific flavor preferences (very berry, ocean splash) for a children's snack he's eating in a wedding hallway, and 'Were you saving it?' as a follow-up question, shows his complete disregard for social norms. Strong character integration — the 'You're a mom, I figured' opener is particularly good.

jokes.text: Michael talking head: 'Ugh. Apricot. Made of real apes.'
jokes.setup: Michael has just eaten a woman's apricot Fruit Roll-Up
jokes.punchline: His complaint about the flavor is the malapropism 'Made of real apes' — mishearing or reinterpreting 'apricot' as ape-related
jokes.explanation: 'Made of real apes' is a wonderfully weird Michael line — a nonsense complaint that suggests he thinks apricot is derived from apes. The non-sequitur confidence of this false etymology is very quotable and specifically Michael's brand of wrong.

jokes.text: Kelly to Ryan: 'Do you think they'll cancel?' Ryan: 'Relax. You'll get your shot at Jim.' Kelly: 'Those two treat the whole office like a 1970s key party.'
jokes.setup: Kelly and Ryan wait for the ceremony and Kelly wonders if the wedding will be called off
jokes.punchline: Kelly's bizarre accusation that Jim and Pam treat the office like a 1970s key party (wife-swapping), which is entirely unexplained and probably groundless
jokes.explanation: Kelly's '1970s key party' comparison is completely unearned and thus very funny — she's built an entire narrative of Jim and Pam as swinging libertines. Ryan's 'You'll get your shot at Jim' confirms his own delusion. The randomness of 'key party' for a sweet couple is perfectly Kelly-paranoid.

jokes.text: Michael's sad talking head: 'I came here hoping to meet somebody. You know, as you do at weddings. End up going to sleep by the vending machine. It was loud, but it was warm.'
jokes.setup: Michael reflects on his romantic hopes for the weekend
jokes.punchline: He slept by the vending machine — 'It was loud, but it was warm' — as if this is a reasonable accommodation he's made peace with
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best Michael moments. 'It was loud, but it was warm' is a perfect line — the resigned acceptance of vending machine warmth as adequate consolation is both deeply sad and very funny. The dignity with which he describes this is characteristic Michael. Highly quotable, strong economy, maximum character integration. Earns 8.

jokes.text: Michael: 'And the love of my life is dating somebody else... It is a terrible year for love.' Then: 'Thinking about having my sperm frozen.'
jokes.setup: Michael continues his sad pre-ceremony talking head
jokes.punchline: His response to romantic despair is to announce he's considering sperm freezing — treating reproductive insurance as the logical response to a bad dating year
jokes.explanation: The pivot from 'terrible year for love' to sperm freezing as a practical contingency plan is classically Michael — treating a romantic problem with an odd clinical solution. Good economy, strong character integration.

jokes.text: Michael is asked by strangers if he has a whoopee cushion — he gives it away: 'There you go. Use it in good health.'
jokes.setup: Two strangers approach Michael asking if he has a whoopee cushion to prank their sister
jokes.punchline: Michael produces one immediately — confirming he brought a whoopee cushion to the wedding — and gifts it with a benediction ('use it in good health')
jokes.explanation: The reveal that Michael brought a whoopee cushion to a wedding is a perfectly natural Michael detail. 'Use it in good health' as a parting gift blessing is a nice touch.

jokes.text: Dwight tries to reclaim wedding gifts from the table: 'What is the etiquette on taking the gift? Can you only take your own back, or is it a whatever-you-can-carry type of thing?' Then tries to trade a toaster for something else.
jokes.setup: The wedding is running very late; Dwight is at the gift table
jokes.punchline: Dwight considers whether it's acceptable to take other people's gifts due to the delay, and then offers to trade a toaster
jokes.explanation: Dwight's pragmatic approach to gift-table economics during the delay is a good character moment. 'Whatever-you-can-carry type of thing' as a gift-taking policy is a funny framing. The toaster barter extension is a solid button.

jokes.text: Toby: 'I'd like to lodge a formal complaint against Jim for making us wait for over an hour.' [said to Dwight while standing at the altar waiting for Jim]
jokes.setup: Jim is missing from his own wedding ceremony; everyone has been waiting over an hour
jokes.punchline: Toby's response is to attempt to file a formal HR complaint against the groom at the altar
jokes.explanation: Toby treating a wedding delay as an HR matter is perfect character comedy. The formality of 'I'd like to lodge a formal complaint' at an altar is an inspired application of his HR role. Strong character integration — this is definitively, irreplaceably Toby. Good economy.

jokes.text: Michael: 'I guess this wedding is not gonna happen. Wonder if this is it for them.' [said casually while the wedding is merely delayed]
jokes.setup: Jim is missing; the ceremony is delayed; people are getting restless
jokes.punchline: Michael immediately jumps to relationship-ending conclusions after a one-hour delay
jokes.explanation: Mild Michael beat — his catastrophizing is in character but doesn't add much beyond expectation. Below average for the episode.

jokes.text: Michael's reaction to Jim and Pam finally arriving: 'S! Yes! I have so much joy in my heart right now. How do I look?'
jokes.setup: Jim and Pam finally arrive to start the ceremony after a long delay
jokes.punchline: Michael immediately pivots from joy to vanity — 'How do I look?' — in the same breath
jokes.explanation: Michael's instant pivot from effusive joy to narcissistic appearance-checking is a good quick beat. The 'S! Yes!' enthusiasm followed by 'how do I look?' is a nice tonal whiplash. Character-specific and economical.

jokes.text: The wedding party walks down the aisle to 'Forever' by Chris Brown — despite Pam and Jim having put it on the 'do not play' list. Jim: 'I begged them not to. I know you specifically put this song on your do not play list.' Pam: 'Yes, I did.' [then they watch and get swept up in it]
jokes.setup: The wedding party enters dancing to a song Pam specifically banned
jokes.punchline: Jim and Pam's initial dismay is replaced by genuine enjoyment — the forbidden song becomes the highlight
jokes.explanation: The JK Wedding Entrance Dance (viral YouTube video parody) is the comedic centerpiece of the episode's third act. The forbidden song becoming the beloved memory is a satisfying character reversal. Works better visually but the setup/release structure is good.

jokes.text: Pam: 'Wait, what happened? You're okay with this?' Jim: 'Yeah, I'm okay.' — Pam is surprised Jim accepts the forbidden song.
jokes.setup: The forbidden song plays and the wedding party starts dancing
jokes.punchline: Jim's acceptance — 'Yeah, I'm okay.' — suggesting he already knew/planned this, or has simply decided to roll with everything
jokes.explanation: Jim's 'Yeah, I'm okay' works because it contains multitudes — it might be Plan B kicking in, or genuine acceptance of chaos. The calm in the center of a comedy storm is very Jim.

jokes.text: Jim talking head: 'I bought those boat tickets the day I saw that YouTube video. I knew we'd need a backup plan. The boat was actually plan C, the church was plan B, and plan A was marrying her a long, long time ago. Pretty much the day I met her.'
jokes.setup: Jim explains the secret Maid of the Mist boat ceremony backup plan
jokes.punchline: His reveal that plan A was 'marrying her a long, long time ago — pretty much the day I met her' reframes the whole episode romantically and serves as the emotional button to the wedding storyline
jokes.explanation: The culminating Jim talking head is funny AND deeply romantic. The A/B/C plan structure (A = 'marrying her the day I met her') is excellent writing — it's both a comedic subversion of the plan-reveal format and a genuinely sweet punchline. Earns 8+ because it's precision storytelling that serves both comedy and emotion simultaneously.

jokes.text: Kevin post-wedding: 'I got six numbers. One more and it would have been a complete telephone number.'
jokes.setup: Kevin reflects on his romantic success at the wedding
jokes.punchline: He got six of the seven digits needed for a phone number — technically significant progress, from his perspective
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best jokes. Kevin's accounting of his romantic success — six digits, one short of a complete phone number — is perfect. The mathematical approach to romantic rejection, and his evident satisfaction at 'six numbers' as a meaningful achievement, is both funny and deeply Kevin. Economy is near-perfect. Highly quotable. Earns 8.

jokes.text: Andy post-wedding: 'My Kleenex shoes were a huge conversation piece, but man, my dogs are barking.'
jokes.setup: Andy's shoes were destroyed; he has apparently used Kleenex as replacement footwear
jokes.punchline: 'My dogs are barking' — his feet hurt from the Kleenex shoes, which he wore to a wedding
jokes.explanation: Wait — this is Andy's shoes, not Kevin's. But it's a callback to the shoe-destruction theme (Kevin's) or more likely Andy had a separate shoe crisis. 'Kleenex shoes' as Andy's solution is a beautifully specific image — the visual of dress-code Kleenex footwear at a wedding is very funny. 'My dogs are barking' in this context is a good old-fashioned expression elevated by the absurd context.

jokes.text: Andy: 'My feet were so sweaty, I can't even feel the cold.' [post-Kleenex shoes]
jokes.setup: Andy discusses the consequences of wearing Kleenex as shoes to a wedding
jokes.punchline: The sweaty feet have rendered his sensory perception of cold impossible — a strange consequence stated with complete matter-of-factness
jokes.explanation: A mild button to the Kleenex shoes joke. The sweat-so-extreme-he-feels-no-cold detail is specific but doesn't add much beyond a passing odd image.

tmdb_overview: The Dunder Mifflin staff head to Niagara Falls for Jim and Pam's wedding, with the understanding that her pregnancy is a forbidden discussion topic, but Jim's slip of the tongue prods Michael to attempt damage control.
